BC_description: All queue and collection methods in the library now throw an error if the 'limit' or 'concurrency' parameter is set to a value less than 1. Previously, passing a value less than 1 may have been allowed or resulted in undefined behavior. The following methods are affected: queue (constructor), priorityQueue (constructor), cargo (constructor), cargoQueue (constructor), mapLimit, eachLimit, filterLimit, reduceLimit, concatLimit, eachOfLimit, forEachOfLimit, groupByLimit. This change ensures that a RangeError is thrown immediately when an invalid limit or concurrency is provided to any of these APIs.
Adaptation_method:
Update all uses of the 'limit' or 'concurrency' parameters in the affected methods to ensure they are set to values greater than or equal to 1. For example:
// Before:
async.mapLimit(arr, 0, iterator, cb)
async.eachLimit(arr, 0, iterator, cb)
async.groupByLimit(arr, 0, iterator, cb)
// After (must be >= 1):
async.mapLimit(arr, 1, iterator, cb)
async.eachLimit(arr, 1, iterator, cb)
async.groupByLimit(arr, 1, iterator, cb)

Passing a value less than 1 (such as 0 or negative numbers) will now throw a RangeError and must be avoided.
